title: Variational Bounds for Perceptron Learning from Structured Data
authors: Francesco Camilli, Pierluigi Contucci, Federica Gerace, Emanuele Mingione
abstract: We introduce a variational approach to a finite-temperature continuous-spin perceptron trained on a Gaussian mixture. The model allows for a broad class of concave utilities and log-concave separable prior measures on the spins. By combining the interpolation method with log-concavity and concentration estimates, we derive lower and upper minimax variational bounds for the limiting quenched pressure. Remarkably, the two bounds differ only in the order of optimization of two variational parameters, while all remaining extrema are controlled by the concave--convex structure of the variational potential. Whenever the two optimizations commute, the two bounds match and identify the solution of the model. The same potential yields the fixed-point equations as stationarity conditions and provides a unified route to the computation of the ground-state energy, training loss, and generalization error.
summary: This work applies sophisticated variational principles from statistical physics to analyze the theoretical performance limits of a continuous-spin perceptron trained on structured data. By deriving matching upper and lower bounds for the quenched pressure, it provides a unified framework to calculate key learning metrics like generalization error and ground-state energy. This connects concepts from machine learning theory directly into the rigorous mathematical tools used in condensed matter physics.
main_problem: The paper derives variational bounds for the quenched pressure associated with Perceptron learning from structured data in the thermodynamic limit.
main_result: Lower and upper minimax variational bounds are established for the limiting quenched pressure, which match when optimization parameters commute, identifying a solution via a single variational principle.
method: The authors employ a variational approach using interpolation techniques (adapted from Guerra and Toninelli) to bound the free energy/quenched pressure.
model_or_system: The model is a continuous-spin perceptron trained on data generated by a Gaussian mixture, described by a random Hamiltonian $H_N(\sigma)$ acting on spins $\sigma \in \mathbb{R}^N$.
key_observables: Quenched pressure (limit of the log partition function), training loss ($\epsilon_t$), generalization error ($\epsilon_g$), and ground-state energy.
important_parameters: Mixing strength ($\lambda$), centroid ($	heta$), regularization parameter ($\kappa$), and system size ($N, M$).
main_assumptions: The method requires specific hypotheses on the utility functions (concavity) and relies on log-concavity estimates; matching of outer optimizations is a key point.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the physical model and Hamiltonian, to introducing variational bounds via interpolation techniques, deriving stationarity conditions from a single potential, and finally applying this framework to compute multiple thermodynamic quantities like loss and error.
why_interesting: Although focused on classical ML models, the use of advanced statistical mechanics tools (variational methods, quenched averages, replica-like structures) mirrors techniques used in analyzing quantum many-body systems near criticality or in disordered quantum Hamiltonians.
